about: Every on-screen label and narration line of the factory video, as claims about the repository it shows. The video is the target. This ledger is the check: verify.mjs fails if a label or line is not here, or if a cited ID or file string does not exist at the build commit, and writes out/claims-report.md with what is built, what is planned and what is open. 'built' cites requirement IDs in specs/ or files that must contain a string. 'planned' cites draft requirement IDs in docs/decisions/. 'open' cites backlog IDs in .tasks/backlog.jsonl. 'illustrative' marks example values that claim nothing.

claims.claim: The scene and its framing
A customer states intent; an engineer captures it as a spec and signs it with a security key and a touch
One engineer signs a spec, two sign the factory, and one signs a release where the tier requires it
labels: One engineer signs a spec, two the factory, one a release by tier.

claims.claim: The agent can write anything but ship nothing: it holds no keys and cannot commit, push to main, tag or sign
The agent works in a cloud session, one run per task
claims.note: Built as the runner producer: one dispatched run per signed task file (SPEC-001-R64), on a GitHub-hosted runner, not a Claude Code cloud session. The cloud session's setup script is versioned since 2026-11-09 (SPEC-001-R211)
labels: cloud session one run per task

claims.claim: Inside the session, a hook flags a test that asserts nothing, and the agent fixes it
claims.note: Built as a project hook: .claude/settings.json runs hook.mjs expect-expect after each Edit or Write. No requirement names the hook, and the runner producer turns hooks off (SPEC-001-R87)

claims.claim: Inside the session, a dependency allowlist stops an unlisted package
claims.note: Built in the pipeline (allowlist check); the in-session hook is planned

claims.claim: The pipeline runs the checks of record without the coding agent
The checks include SAST, SCA and secret scanning
The checks include DAST
claims.note: Decision 0006 G3 recommends recording DAST as not applicable and dropping the chip; the owner has not decided

claims.claim: A scope check fails any path outside the task
claims.note: Built as a thin check (SPEC-001-R66): it judges every commit that carries a Task: trailer, and the publish job adds one to every runner delivery. A commit without the trailer is not judged; the full rule waits for an owner decision

claims.claim: Tests are proven to catch broken code: property tests and a mutation threshold that cannot be lowered
Scoped AI checks can fail a change, never pass one, and a failure sticks to the change
labels: checks of record · AI can only fail

claims.claim: The patch lands on a candidate branch and is promoted to main out of the agent's reach
labels: promote to main out of reach

claims.claim: Only the pipeline signs the evidence and holds the deploy key
labels: pipeline signs the evidence, holds the key

claims.claim: Where the tier requires it, an engineer who did not write the spec checks staging, then signs the release
Free text from customers, agents, docs and URLs is untrusted and never starts a run
Poisoned issue #4821 stops at the sandbox wall
An issue becomes work only through a spec an engineer signs and a task; known errors start from alarms the signed policy already maps
claims.note: The signed task file and its check are built (SPEC-001-R64, R65). The rule that agent commits need a task is thin: only commits with a Task: trailer are judged. Alarm-started work is planned
labels: Engineer checks it against the specs

claims.claim: An issue's free text is a quarantined notes field that no agent receives
The receipt records where a change began and traces it from intent to deploy
claims.note: Built as SPEC-001-R55's seven lines (COMMIT, FILES, AGENT, MODEL, SPEC, SIGNED, VERIFIED), with MODEL always 'not recorded'. INTENT, TASK and AUTHOR are planned for Tracer 2 slice T3; FACTORY, the checks, DEPLOY, ORIGIN and TRIGGER come later

claims.claim: Production telemetry is untrusted; a quarantined reader fills a fixed schema, and its free text never reaches the agent
Only an alarm named in the signed policy can start an approved task
A separate security account watches the pipeline and production for drift, and the pipeline cannot touch it
Production opens only for a change whose evidence is complete
labels: The agent advises. The pipeline acts.
